subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should maintainers authorize a narrow security-reviewed repair that aligns the embedded streaming scanner with the shared reasoning-tag grammar for this issue?
rationale: The code change is small, but it affects a sensitive user-visible privacy boundary and the issue is already marked no-new-fix-pr and needs security review, so automation should not open a fix PR without maintainer intent.

options.title: Authorize narrow sanitizer repair
options.body: Fix the embedded scanner, add focused streamed attribute-bearing tag tests, and require proof that normal delivery hides reasoning while explicit reasoning presentation still works.

options.title: Keep manual-only until live proof
options.body: Wait for a maintainer or reporter to provide a fresh affected-channel run before allowing code changes, accepting that the source-level mismatch remains open.

options.title: Move under a broader delivery tracker
options.body: Only redirect this issue if maintainers explicitly decide the broader channel-delivery work will own this exact embedded scanner gap.

recommendation.title: Authorize narrow sanitizer repair
recommendation.body: Fix the embedded scanner, add focused streamed attribute-bearing tag tests, and require proof that normal delivery hides reasoning while explicit reasoning presentation still works.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue needs a security/default-boundary decision, and this person has central history in the shared reasoning sanitizer and was mentioned in the issue timeline as a routing candidate.
